title: Sam Altman at Stanford (2015): founder traits, hiring late, pivots, and avoiding fake work
summary: Sam Altman, then YC president, explains what he looks for in founders and how startups win or fail. Themes: clarity of vision, speed, determination, co-founder dynamics, hiring as late as possible, pursuing good ideas that look bad, getting users who love you, and avoiding fake work.

principles.text: Founders must explain clearly what they do and why; unclear vision means they can't recruit, sell, or think well.
principles.quote: if the founder can't explain it clearly to us then a they're never going to be able to recruit hire sell talk to the press anything

principles.text: Hire as late as possible; early employees add burn, inertia and politics and reduce effectiveness.
principles.quote: our best startups hire the least and our worst startups are the ones that want to say I have 10 people working for me I'm really cool

principles.text: Chase great ideas that look bad, not derivatives of the last winner; look for a shift in the world.
principles.quote: what is the next hundred billion company that has nothing to do with the last um what is the shift in the world

principles.text: Ignore everyone except users; launch quickly so users who depend on you give you conviction.
principles.quote: you can ignore everybody if you you can ignore everybody except users

principles.text: Focus on product means building love in a small group of users, not mild liking from many.
principles.quote: focus on product means focus on love not like

principles.text: Avoid fake work like fundraising, press and networking; the real work is building and talking to users.
principles.quote: no company has ever become great because they were great at fundraising
